units.why: Instructors should remind students "never to upload personally identifiable information, passwords, health information, protected UMN data", a data-protection rule (P50).

units.passage: input student work into GenAI tools without the student’s explicit written consent, and all materials must be anonymized, regardless of whether they are used for instructional or research purposes.
units.why: Instructors "should never input student work into GenAI tools without the student's explicit written consent" and must anonymize it, a student-data protection rule (P50).

units.passage: Do not enter private, sensitive, or copyrighted information
units.why: "Do not enter private, sensitive, or copyrighted information" into AI systems protects personal and confidential data (P50).

units.passage: [I will not upload your work to any GenAI tools for teaching or research purposes without your written consent and any work uploaded will be fully anonymized]
units.why: The instructor promises "any work uploaded will be fully anonymized", a data-protection limit on instructor AI use (P50).

units.passage: Data classified as Public data can be used freely in generative AI platforms.
units.why: Public data "can be used freely in generative AI platforms", which sets the data-protection boundary by classification (P50).

units.passage: Safeguarding data means only uploading allowed University data into appropriately licensed tools.
units.why: "only uploading allowed University data into appropriately licensed tools" protects data and steers use to licensed tools (P50).

units.passage: you can and can't add to AI tools.
units.why: A table lists, for each licensed tool, which data classes (public, restricted, highly restricted, health) can be added to AI tools, a data-protection rule (P50).
units.fit_note: Tool-by-tool, data-class-by-data-class permissions in a table. / A tool-by-data-class matrix; the anchor only introduces it.

units.passage: It is prohibited to use private student information as defined by the Board of Regents Student Education Records policy in AI tools that are not UMN licensed.
units.why: "It is prohibited to use private student information ... in AI tools that are not UMN licensed" protects student data and favors licensed tools (P50).

units.passage: It is against University policy to use data classified as Private-Highly Restricted or Private-Restricted
units.why: Using restricted data in unlicensed tools is "against University policy", a data-protection rule (P50).

units.passage: However, when it comes to using AI, it’s important to understand how to protect data and use the tools appropriately in your role at the University.
units.why: "it’s important to understand how to protect data and use the tools appropriately in your role" asks users to protect data: P50.

units.passage: Please be aware, too, that AI detection tools are often unreliable, and use of AI detection software, which is not FERPA-protected, may violate students’ privacy or intellectual property rights.
units.why: "use of AI detection software, which is not FERPA-protected, may violate students' privacy or intellectual property rights" is a privacy and IP warning about detector software. P50 is nearest; P39 is about reliability, which the previous unit covers.
units.fit_note: Warns about privacy and IP risk of detector software for student work, not AI tools storing prompts. Warns instructors about detector software for privacy and IP reasons; the type is about protecting data in general.

units.passage: AI tools and services should be viewed as posting data on a public website
units.why: Frames AI tools as "posting data on a public website", a privacy principle that tells users what to assume when using a tool; P50 (protect data) fits better than P56 because the point is data exposure.

units.passage: Only publicly available information (data that has no legal or other requirement for confidentiality, integrity, or availability under the Freedom of Information Act) may be used in generative AI tools and services
units.policy: Only publicly available information (data with no legal or other requirement for confidentiality, integrity, or availability under the Freedom of Information Act) may be used in generative AI tools and services.
units.why: "Only publicly available information ... may be used" in AI tools is a data-use limit binding all users; 'Only' turns the permission into a requirement, so must. P50 (protect confidential data), not P49, because it concerns any non-public data.

units.passage: Users should expect these AI tools and services to use input data for its training, including the derivative use of any data submitted
units.why: Warns users to "expect these AI tools and services to use input data for its training", a fact about tool data practices supporting the privacy rule; P50 covers "AI tools store prompts".
